64169c8c9e3e95678dcd0fe8ef71a1bbd5298056.summary: Socket reports 13 malicious NuGet packages, published between July and November 2026, used in fake .NET developer job assessments built on WinUI 3. Building or running the lure triggers a build-time MSBuild stager, a DLL side-loading setup around the Windows On-Screen Keyboard, and a downloader in a button control that fetches executables from GitHub. Related components include a GitHub-based command and control loader, a Chrome profile stealer and a trojanized wallet analyzer app. The report does not attribute the campaign to a named threat actor.

hedges: The report has not attributed this campaign to a named threat actor; resemblance to North Korean fake job interview operations is noted only.
The report could not determine how the Home Assessment lures reach candidates.
The DLL side-load was not tested, and whether a copied osk.exe starts from that folder on current Windows builds is an open question.
Several repositories and accounts returned 404 during analysis, so later stages are unknown.
Download counts include mirrors and scanners and are not victim counts.
Timing links between packages and repositories are treated as timing evidence only.
The report could not determine whether one GitHub repository belongs to the threat actor or to a targeted developer.
Links between the button packages and the rest of the cluster rest on naming and technique, not shared indicators.
